real_situations.problem: XP/7 HMI works but cannot be reinstalled.
real_situations.solution: Disk image it, isolate it, keep it as reference, and build a read-only dashboard beside it.

real_situations.problem: PLC software and license are gone.
real_situations.solution: Avoid bypassing licenses; recover backups, contact OEM, document behavior, and plan replacement.
Identify baud/parity/stop bits, observe traffic, decode frames, then build a reader before any command.
Run shadow monitoring first, test during scheduled windows, and keep rollback ready.

rs232_lesson.meaning: Simulated pySerial loopback frame for press current register 40003; no real COM port is opened by default.
rs232_lesson.warning: Real RS-232/RFC2217 links are not encrypted or authenticated; use only in trusted, authorized environments.

workflow.meaning: Record PLC, HMI, I/O cards, cables, firmware, software, and machine drawings.
Clone the old PC drive and preserve PLC/HMI backups where authorized.
Place XP/7 and legacy PLC behind OT firewall/VLAN; keep internet away.
Read registers/signals only; confirm values against operators and maintenance.
Compare extracted Ladder, HMI screens, alarm list, and machine behavior.
Publish safe historian/dashboard data without commanding the machine.
Plan HMI/PLC replacement with FAT, SAT, cutover, and rollback.
